results.claim: For every Gaussian block law p_{mu,sigma} in the standardized null rectangle |mu|<=h, ell<=sigma<=u, write p_Ubar=(p_{-h,u}+p_{+h,u})/2 and p_rho=rho p_Lbar+(1-rho)p_Ubar. Using cosh(z)>=exp(|z|)/2 and maximizing the resulting concave quadratic in |ybar| gives the exact analytic envelope p_{mu,sigma}/p_Ubar <= 2 (u/ell)^m exp(m h^2/(2u^2)). Therefore p_{mu,sigma}/p_rho <= M(rho):=[2/(1-rho)](u/ell)^m exp(m h^2/(2u^2)). Uniformly for rho<=0.56, M<=461.24628. This removes the need for an empirical pointwise-ratio search in the tail argument.

For C(mu,sigma)=E_q[p_{mu,sigma}/p_rho], C_mumu has kernel H_mu=m^2(ybar-mu)^2/sigma^4-m/sigma^2. H_mu is nonnegative whenever |ybar-mu|>=sigma/sqrt(m). Hence any |ybar|>B_mu:=h+u/sqrt(m)=0.29577714 contributes nonnegatively for every null parameter and may be dropped in a lower bound. For the remaining W-tail, negative H_mu is bounded below by -m/ell^2, so for any R, C_mumu >= integral_{|ybar|<=B, W<=R} q(p_theta/p_rho)H_mu - M m/ell^2 P_q(W>R), for any B>=B_mu. Under the frozen NIG hierarchy, W/4 is exactly BetaPrime((m-1)/2,3), so P_q(W>R)=I_{4/(R+4)}(3,(m-1)/2). With rho<=0.56 and R=2000, the entire omitted negative-tail penalty is <=0.09809. Thus the unbounded NIG tail is no longer a substantive proof blocker for C_mumu.

For t=log sigma, C_tt has kernel H_t(z)=z^2-2(m+1)z+m^2 with z=[W+m(ybar-mu)^2]/sigma^2. Its upper zero is z_+=m+1+sqrt(2m+1)=41.06225775 and H_t>=0 for z>=z_+. Therefore every point outside the fixed compact domain W<=z_+u^2=47.40966879 and |ybar|<=h+u sqrt(z_+/m)=1.32301839 contributes nonnegatively for every null parameter. Consequently C_tt is lower-bounded by the integral over this compact rectangle with exactly zero tail penalty. No predictive-tail truncation theorem is needed for the log-scale second derivative.

Independent deterministic Gauss-Legendre sufficient-statistic quadrature, used only as engineering evidence, retained large margins after the rigorous compactification. Over a 31x41 parameter grid the compact mean-curvature integral on |ybar|<=1,W<=2000 had minimum about 30.80 before the <=0.0981 exact tail penalty; continuous numerical optimization put the compact minimum near mu=0,sigma=0.9993 at about 30.796. For log-scale curvature, the fixed tail-free compact integral had numerical minimum about 19.605 near mu=0,sigma=u. These are not interval-certified values, but they show the compact proof problem retains large slack.

negative_or_scope_evidence: The four-corner factor is still not promoted: compact-domain integrals are not yet interval/direct-rounding certified over the parameter continuum.
The deterministic quadrature minima are engineering evidence only and do not replace a rigorous lower enclosure.
The ratio envelope is deliberately conservative; its purpose is proof-safe tail control, not tight power prediction.

All statements remain restricted to the r86/r87 standardized m=32 frozen NIG predictor and iid Gaussian null rectangle; no heavy-tail, serial-dependence, gradual-drift or repeated-change guarantee follows.
frontier: Interval-certify the now-compact C_mumu lower integral on |ybar|<=1,W<=2000 and subtract the exact <=0.0981 beta-prime tail penalty; the numerical margin is about 30.8.
Interval-certify the tail-free C_tt lower integral on |ybar|<=1.3231,W<=47.41; the numerical margin is about 19.6.
Exploit the compact domains to derive finite parameter-transport/Lipschitz bounds and reduce interval cells before doing high-precision quadrature.
If both curvature signs certify, solve rho with a directed-rounding bracket and verify active-corner directional expectations; only then promote q/p_rho over r85 UI.
exact_next_action: Replace the former unbounded-tail interval plan with two compact validated-numerics problems. First certify C_tt on the fixed small rectangle, where omitted mass is provably nonnegative. Then certify C_mumu on |ybar|<=1,W<=2000 and subtract the exact beta-prime negative-tail penalty <=0.0981. Use coarse parameter cells first because the engineering margins remain >19 and >30; derive interval derivative bounds only if direct interval quadrature over parameter boxes is too wide.
